leads.name: Chris Reed
leads.post: Looking for feedback re changing to dripless seals on our 3650 ACMY. Current Mercruiser 8.1s, shop pulling shafts for inspection and packing replacement on conventional drip stuffing boxes. Option to go to dripless - any experience pros/cons for the price?
leads.flag: Chris has a 3650 ACMY sitting at a yard right now with the shafts pulled — an owner actively spending on the boat and facing a real decision this week, which is exactly the window to be useful. The play is a genuinely helpful answer on dripless vs. repacking (the labor overlap is the whole economics of the choice), not a pitch. Owners mid-refit are the ones who call a broker a year later, and this is the same group Rich Redmond posted in, so Zach showing up helpful twice compounds. Don't sell anything here.
leads.dm:
Hey Chris. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Cruisers Yachts Owners group.

Since the shop already has the shafts out, most of the labor for a dripless swap is money you're spending anyway — that's usually the only time the conversion really pencils out. That said, if your stuffing boxes are in good shape, fresh packing is cheap and any yard anywhere can service it.

Is she your long-term boat, or do you see yourself moving up at some point?

leads.name: Wayne Rambo
leads.post:
2023 42 Cantius owner here. Purchased the boat used back in February. I have owned several bowriders and center consoles in the past, but not one with these Volvo IPS engines and pods.

The last two times out, when I started throttling up to cruise speed, I got an alert that the transmission filter was clogged, and had to throttle back… I have now replaced both oil filters on the transmissions…

I would like to check the transmission oil level, but apparently there is no dipstick on these D6-IPS500 drives… Anyone with a similar vessel with advice on where to find the transmission oil level reading?
leads.flag: Bought in February, first IPS boat, recurring alert that's cutting his outings short — and no dealer relationship yet. He's a recent buyer of a high-value boat who doesn't yet have a trusted person to call. That's a relationship opening, not a transaction.
leads.dm:
Hey Wayne. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Cruisers Cantius Owners group.

Sorry you're dealing with that in your first season with her. There's no dipstick on those IPS drives—the level reads through the EVC display, though the menu path varies by software version.

That said, a clog alarm right after fresh filters is worth a VODIA scan at a Volvo dealer before you chase the level. Where are you keeping her?

leads.name: Erick Calderon
leads.post: The boat is now 4 years old….the starboard and the port engines trim motors stopped working….is this a common occurrence? Any preventive measures?
leads.flag: Both trim motors failing at four years, and the ellipses read as frustration rather than curiosity. Owners who start questioning whether their boat's failures are "normal" are early in the process that ends with a listing. Worth answering well and remembering.
leads.dm:
Hey Erick. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Regal 38XO/FXO/GC & Fly Owners group.

Sorry you're dealing with that—four years is early for trim trouble.

Both sides quitting at once usually isn't the motors. Check the trim relays and harness connections first; corrosion there takes out both sides together and looks exactly like dead motors. When you hit the switch, do you hear a click?

leads.name: Jon Edenfield
leads.post:
YACHT SENSE module not detected???

New as 50 fly owner here. My yacht sense app was working however now when I touch the app, it says yacht sense module not detected.

Where is the yacht sense module located? I can't find it behind the helm… Is there some breaker or switch that needs to be on to activate it?

I do have two UPSs that I think may feed the network switch.
leads.flag: New owner of a 50 Fly, systems he hasn't learned yet, and he's guessing at his own electrical layout. Same profile as Wayne — recent buyer without a go-to person. Answer this well and he remembers who helped in week one.
leads.dm:
Hey Jon. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Azimut Yacht Owners group.

Welcome to the 50. "Module not detected" after the app was working is almost always network power, not a dead module.

Before pulling panels, power the network switch down for thirty seconds and bring it back, and confirm both UPSs are actually up rather than on bypass. How's she treating you otherwise?

leads.name: Benjamin Antonio Castro Rivera
leads.post:
We recently purchased a Yamaha 6 HP 4-stroke outboard for our inflatable tender. Since we often spend a couple of nights anchored in bays throughout the Caribbean, we use the tender quite a bit…

However, we haven't found a good permanent storage solution for the outboard while we're underway. We would prefer not to leave it mounted on the tender, and we're looking for a secure location or perhaps a custom bracket, mount, or rack somewhere on the boat.

Has anyone come up with a practical solution?
leads.flag: Cruising the Caribbean on a 38XO and solving a real problem. No transaction in it, but this is an engaged, active owner in a brand group — the kind of person whose recommendation carries weight later.
leads.dm:
Hey Benjamin. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Regal 38XO/FXO/GC & Fly Owners group.

The two setups that hold up are a through-bolted rail mount with a backing plate, or a padded chock in the lazarette with a strap. Storing it upright also sidesteps Yamaha's resting-side rule that can push oil into the cylinder.

For the Caribbean, a cover on the powerhead earns its keep. How are you lifting it aboard now?

leads.name: Darcy Hughes
leads.post:
So the old, poorly manufactured, adjustment lever for the flybridge helm seat on my 2006 Azimut 55fly has failed. I purchased a replacement from Marine Max, but the lever casing is just a little too small to swap over so I'm trying to replace the whole slide rail mechanism. Unfortunately, it is glued down with what appears to be the same white stuff in all the seams of the superstructure.

Does anyone have any good tips or tricks on how to get this stainless steel slide unglued from the fiberglass tub?
leads.flag: Straight DIY question with no transaction behind it. Answering it well costs one message and earns standing in an Azimut owners' group, which is exactly the room worth being known in.
leads.dm:
Hey Darcy. How's it going? My name is Zach Hassell. I came across your post in the Azimut Yacht Owners group.

Sorry you're fighting that—the white stuff is almost certainly 3M 5200 or a Sika equivalent, and it's structural.

Heat gun on low along the bond line, then cut underneath with braided fishing line rather than prying—levering against the fiberglass usually costs gelcoat. A polyurethane debonder helps if it's stubborn. Did the new rail come with a bedding spec?
